How much is a used Levi's 501 jeans worth?

Most used Levi's 501s are worth little, but some vintage pairs sell for a lot. The tags tell you which one you have.

Updated 2026-11-06 · by FlipLens

Which one do you have?

Look at the red tab, the care tag and the button. A capital "E" on the red tab ("Big E") marks pairs from before the early 1970s, which are collectible. Pairs made in the USA are generally more sought after than recent ones. The waist and length are on the leather or paper patch at the back.

What decides the price

  • Age and origin: vintage, Big E and Made in USA pairs above recent ones.
  • Size: common sizes sell faster; vintage sizes run smaller than labelled.
  • Fades and wear: natural fades are valued, but holes in the crotch lower the price.
  • Fit: 501 versus other cuts such as 505 or 550.

Check before you buy

  • Read the red tab, care tag, button and patch.
  • Measure the waist and length flat.
  • Check the crotch and pockets for holes.

Where it sells best

Recent 501s sell on Vinted for small amounts. Vintage pairs sell on eBay and vintage marketplaces: put "vintage", the decade and the origin in the title.

Questions

How much is a used Levi's 501 jeans worth?

It depends on age, origin, size and fades. Prices change weekly, so check today's value: type "Levi's 501 jeans" and the condition into FlipLens (fliplens.eu), which compares current eBay listings in the UK and five EU countries and shows the expected sale price and the most worth paying.

How do I know if my Levi's 501 are vintage?

Check the red tab (a capital E means early pairs), the care tag and the country of origin. Older pairs often have no long care tag at all.

Are modern Levi's 501 worth reselling?

Only when bought cheaply. They sell steadily but for modest amounts.
